title: Kth Largest Element In a Stream
description:
Track the kth largest entry in a growing stream of integers, counting repeated values as separate entries.

Implement the KthLargest class:

  • __init__(k: int, nums: list[int]) initializes the stream with nums and fixes its rank k.
  • add(val: int) -> int inserts val, then returns the kth largest entry in the stream after that insertion.

Every add call occurs when the resulting stream has at least k entries. Equal numbers occupy separate ranks; the constructor reports null rather than a rank.

You are graded on a recorded sequence of calls on one live object. The first call names the class and passes constructor arguments; subsequent calls name methods and their arguments. The constructor and methods returning nothing report null; the result array has one entry per call.

Constraints:

  • 1 <= k <= 10000.
  • Initially 0 to 10000 numbers, each between -10000 and 10000.
  • At most 10000 add calls; use O(log k) work per insertion.

Example 1:

Calls: ["KthLargest","add","add","add","add","add"]
Arguments: [[3,[4,5,8,2]],[3],[5],[10],[9],[4]]
Output: [null,4,5,5,8,8]

The third-largest entries after each insertion are 4, 5, 5, 8, and 8.

Example 2:

Calls: ["KthLargest","add","add","add"]
Arguments: [[1,[]],[-2],[0],[-5]]
Output: [null,-2,0,0]

With k equal to one, the answer is the largest value seen so far.

Example 3:

Calls: ["KthLargest","add","add","add"]
Arguments: [[2,[5,5]],[5],[6],[4]]
Output: [null,5,5,5]

Duplicate fives take separate ranks; six becomes first while five stays second.

The first add makes the stream large enough to have a third entry.
Adding a low value leaves rank two unchanged; a higher value raises it.
Tied maxima still rank as individual entries.
After a high insertion rank four rises, but a low insertion cannot lower it.
Negative values use the same descending order.
Repeated values count toward rank three.
Each insertion supplies a new candidate; after the first insertion the second-largest rank is defined.
